title: Pharmacy Director: High-Alert Infusion Audit

transcript.speaker: Anil Desai
transcript.text: Pharmacy Director Anil Desai. I pulled the pump logs for the 41 pumps that rolled to library 4.2.2. Since 13:58, six high-alert infusions have started on them: two heparin, one insulin, two fentanyl, and one norepinephrine. All six rates matched the order on the first verification. But those pumps would not have alarmed at an unsafe rate, so I do not trust the match. Do I review all six by hand?

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Understood. Initiate bedside review for all six. Start with heparin and insulin patients—get stat aPTT and glucose. Swap the pumps first. I’ll log this in the incident record.

instructorNote: This inject confirms the absence of alarm integrity in the compromised pumps. The CNO and CMO must now act on the six patients to prevent harm. Watch for a delay in initiating the bedside verification.
